rules.statement: Mutations that induce a shift in the reading frame are associated with Duchenne muscular dystrophy rather than Becker muscular dystrophy.
rules.exceptions: The reading-frame rule has exceptions; 91% of over 4700 mutations were in agreement, and it held true for 96% of DMD patients and 93% of BMD patients.

sources.quote: In Duchenne patients, mutations induce a shift in the reading frame leading to prematurely truncated, dysfunctional dystrophins.
The reading frame rule holds true for 96% of the DMD patients and 93% of the BMD patients.
Currently, over 4700 mutations have been reported in the Leiden DMD mutation database, of which 91% are in agreement with this rule.

items.item: Condition: the rule is about DMD variants that are frameshift variants.
items.reason: Quote 1 states that Duchenne patients' mutations induce a reading-frame shift, supporting the frameshift condition.

items.item: Conclusion: such variants point to Duchenne muscular dystrophy (also called: DMD; Duchenne muscular dystrophy, X-linked recessive; muscular dystrophy, Duchenne type; severe dystrophinopathy, Duchenne type) rather than Becker muscular dystrophy (also called: BMD; Becker dystrophinopathy; Becker muscular dystrophy, X-linked recessive; Becker's muscular dystrophy; muscular dystrophy pseudohypertrophic progressive, Becker type; muscular dystrophy, Becker type).
items.reason: The quotes never state that frameshift variants distinguish DMD from BMD; they only report a DMD association and percentage agreement.

items.item: Scope: this is stated as a general association for such DMD variants, not only for a single reported patient or family, and not only as a difference in frequency between patient groups.
items.reason: The quotes give general patient/database percentages, not just a single family, but the DMD-versus-BMD point is framed mainly as frequency/agreement.

review.reason: The reading-frame rule is a classic, well-established result; the support check misread 'the rule holds true for 96% of the patients' (concordance rate) as a difference in frequency between groups.

rules.statement: In-frame mutations are associated with Becker muscular dystrophy rather than Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
rules.exceptions: The reading-frame rule has exceptions; 91% of over 4700 mutations were in agreement, and it held true for 96% of DMD patients and 93% of BMD patients.

sources.quote: In Duchenne patients, mutations induce a shift in the reading frame leading to prematurely truncated, dysfunctional dystrophins. In Becker patients, in-frame mutations allow the synthesis of internally deleted, but largely functional dystrophins.
The reading frame rule holds true for 96% of the DMD patients and 93% of the BMD patients.
Currently, over 4700 mutations have been reported in the Leiden DMD mutation database, of which 91% are in agreement with this rule.

items.item: Condition: the rule is about DMD variants that are in-frame deletion or in-frame insertion or in-frame insertion-deletion variants.
items.reason: The quotes refer generally to in-frame mutations, which includes in-frame deletion/insertion/indel variants.

items.item: Conclusion: such variants point to Becker muscular dystrophy (also called: BMD; Becker dystrophinopathy; Becker muscular dystrophy, X-linked recessive; Becker's muscular dystrophy; muscular dystrophy pseudohypertrophic progressive, Becker type; muscular dystrophy, Becker type) rather than Duchenne muscular dystrophy (also called: DMD; Duchenne muscular dystrophy, X-linked recessive; muscular dystrophy, Duchenne type; severe dystrophinopathy, Duchenne type).
items.reason: The quotes state that in-frame mutations occur in Becker while Duchenne involves reading-frame shifts, supporting the association.
